metadata.title: Nexus Between Financial Deepening and Stability of Financial Sector in Nigeria
metadata.description: ABSTRACT: Extant studies focused on investigating the relationship between financial deepening and aggregate economy with no consideration for whether or not financial deepening is responsible for or affects financial sector’s stability. Sequel to the foregoing, this study examined the nature of causation between financial deepening and financial sector’s stability with special interest in the direction of causality between the two. Financial sector’s stability (FSSI) was proxied with bank z-score while financial deepening by deposit money banks (FDDMB), Central Bank of Nigeria (FDCBN), insurance sector (FDINS), financial market (FDSTM) and the entire financial system (FSD) was proxied with the ratio of the bank assets to GDP, ratio of the Bank assets to GDP, ratio of insurance assets to GDP, the ratio of market capitalization to GDP and financial system deposit as a percentage of GDP respectively. Time series data were collected from the World Bank development database for the period between 1999 and 2021 and were analysed by employing Autoregressive Distributed Lags Model following the integration of the study’s variables at I(0) and I(1). Although, the result revealed that most of the proxies of financial deepening showed positive but insignificant relationship with financial sector’s stability in Nigeria: FDINS (p-value = 0.3181>0.5), FDSTM (p-value =0.6477>0.5), FSD (0.6565>0.5); FDCBN was negative and insignificant with p-value = 0.0939>0.5. However, financial deepening by the deposit money banks was the only significant predictor with p-value = 0.0365<0.05. Furthermore, the causality test revealed that there was an element of bidirectional causality between the financial deepening and financial sector’s stability in Nigeria. This means that financial deepening causes financial sector’s stability and vice versa. Consequently, the study concluded that there is a mutual cause and effect relationship between the financial deepening and financial stability in the Nigerian banking sector and recommended aggressive deposit mobilization among others by the both bank and non-bank financial agents, so as to further deepen finance and stabilize Nigerian financial sector.
keywords: Causality, Banking Stability, Insurance, Stock Market, Gross Domestic Product

metadata.title: Reproducibility package for: Local-annihilator relation codes and algebraic reflexivity of nonsingular three-spaces in M4 over finite fields
metadata.description:
Exact finite-field verification programs, unit tests, and deterministic machine-readable certificates accompanying version 29 of the article:

Local-annihilator relation codes and algebraic reflexivity of nonsingular three-spaces in M4 over finite fields

by Saofee Busaman, Kittisak Tinpun, and Chanpen Phokaew.

The archive reproduces and independently audits the article’s computational results, including:

• the algebraic-reflexivity classification of the seven Gordon–Lunardon–Shaw classes of nonsingular three-dimensional subspaces of M4(F2), including the sharp value f_F2(3) = 4;
• relation-code weight enumerators and generalized-weight hierarchies distinguishing all seven binary classes;
• the hyperplane trichotomy for the three nonsingular four-dimensional binary sections;
• an exhaustive rational-canonical-form census of 789,624 normalized surviving ternary generator pairs, independently confirming reflexivity for every nonsingular three-space in M4(F3);
• an independent audit of 2,880 hyperplanes obtained from the published order-81 semifield representatives and their tensor-axis permutations; and
• reduced 5-by-4 and 6-by-4 non-square binary equality examples.

The ternary theorem in the article has a symbolic proof and does not depend on this computation. All computational decisions use exact finite-field arithmetic. In the exhaustive ternary census, independent exact code paths for determinants, local annihilators, and ranks agree in every case. SHA-256 and BLAKE2b-256 digests certify the census output, and PAYLOAD_SHA256SUMS.txt verifies every archived payload file.

Run the verification programs from the extracted archive root. The reproducibility guide REPRODUCIBILITY.md specifies the required Python environment, commands, expected results, runtime information, certificate scope, and integrity checks.

metadata.title: BRIDGING THE COMPUTATIONAL GAP: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A CUSTOM WEB CORPUS TOOL
metadata.description: The integration of corpus linguistics into Translation Studies (TS) is widely recognized as a methodological necessity for evaluating and improving automated translation systems. However, a significant software barrier persists: commercial platforms impose prohibitive subscription costs, while open-source Python libraries require advanced programming expertise. This paper details the software architecture and computational engineering of a custom-built, open-source web application designed to bridge this gap. Developed using the Flask microframework and integrating the spaCy Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipeline, the platform provides zero-installation access to advanced analytical features. The architectural design includes a multi-stage document ingestion pipeline capable of optical character recognition (OCR) for scanned PDFs, chunked processing for memory-efficient text parsing, and a JSON-based inverted index for rapid data retrieval. By engineering complex functionalities such as Parallel Concordancing, Corpus Query Language (CQL) parsing, and automated web-scraping within an intuitive graphical interface, this platform provides a highly scalable computational infrastructure for data-driven translation research.

metadata.title: The network that learned to run itself
metadata.description: The limitations of traditional automation with scale and complexity have given rise to a powerful new concept - hyper-automation - Mostly for IT and cybersecurity areas. It is a system that allows machines to be self-managed and self-adaptive through AI, machine learning, and software orchestration, reducing human intervention. Streaming services, IoT sensors, and remote works are just some of the main drivers that bring about the need to shift traditional rule-based automation to proactive, self-regulating networks, which are enabled by real-time monitoring and decision-making like, for example, congestion prevention and resource allocation done autonomously by AIOps tools. So, 24x7 security, with minimum downtime and human error, is possible to achieve by organizations. Meanwhile, the reliance on autonomous systems creates important questions about trust responsibility accountability and Because of this, the necessity of effective oversight as well as the presence of highly trained personnel who are capable of handling these technologies will become paramount to the equation. Businesses that implement hyper-automation [1] well may end up far ahead of the competitors that still rely on manual processes. It just goes to show that as the network landscape evolves, the organizations that are going to thrive are the ones adopting hyper-automation at a deep level. In the end, getting on board with hyper-automation is not only a futuristic consideration, it is a requirement for organizations who desire to be competitive in the digital world.[14][15][16][17]
